cards.title: What is Documentation in Insurance?
cards.content: Documentation in insurance refers to all the forms, documents, certificates, and written records used throughout the insurance process — from applying for insurance to receiving the claim. The FIRST STAGE of documentation is the PROPOSAL FORM.

cards.title: Complete List of Insurance Documents (in order)
cards.content: The documents used in the insurance process are: (1) Proposal Form, (2) Acceptance of Proposal, (3) Premium Receipt, (4) Cover Note, (5) Certificate of Insurance, (6) Policy Document, (7) Warranty, (8) Endorsement, (9) Renewal Notice.

cards.title: What is the Proposal Form?
cards.content: The Proposal Form is the FIRST STAGE of documentation. Through the proposal form, the insured provides all necessary information about the subject matter to be insured. It is the starting point of the entire insurance process.

cards.title: Declaration in Proposal Form
cards.content: The insurance company adds a DECLARATION at the END of the proposal form which is SIGNED BY THE INSURED. This declaration confirms that all information provided is true and complete.

cards.title: Elements of a Proposal Form
cards.content: A proposal form includes: (1) Full name of the proposer, (2) Address and contact details, (3) Profession of the proposer, (4) Sum Insured, (5) Previous and present insurance details, (6) Loss experience (past claims history), (7) Declaration by the insured.

cards.title: Material Fact
cards.content: MATERIAL FACT is complete and correct information about the subject matter to be insured. It is important because it INFLUENCES THE DECISION OF THE UNDERWRITER — whether to accept the risk, at what rate, and on what terms. Without proper material facts, underwriting cannot be done correctly.

cards.title: Fire Insurance Proposal — What Information is Required
cards.content: For a FIRE INSURANCE proposal, the following information is needed: (1) Process of manufacturing, (2) Details of materials contained/stored, (3) Construction of the building. ALL THREE of these are required — not just one.

sections.title: 🧑💼 Agent as Intermediary and Primary Underwriter

cards.title: Role of Insurance Agent
cards.content: The Insurance Agent (also called Advisor) acts as an INTERMEDIARY between the insurer and the insured. The agent is also called the PRIMARY UNDERWRITER or FIELD UNDERWRITER because the agent collects all necessary information and fills the proposal form — the first step of underwriting.

cards.title: Underwriting Process
cards.content: The process of SCRUTINIZING (thoroughly examining) the proposal form and deciding about acceptance is called UNDERWRITING. The insurance company's underwriter reviews the proposal and decides whether to accept the risk, at what premium, and on what terms.

cards.title: IRDAI Processing Time
cards.content: As per IRDAI guidelines, an insurance company must process an insurance proposal within 15 DAYS of receipt.

cards.title: What is Premium?
cards.content: PREMIUM is the CONSIDERATION — the amount paid by the INSURED to the INSURER for insuring the subject matter under the contract. It is the price of insurance.

cards.title: How Can Premium Be Paid?
cards.content: Premium payment modes: (1) CASH, (2) CHEQUE, (3) ONLINE/Digital payment, (4) CREDIT CARD. Premium CANNOT be collected through a PROMISSORY NOTE. Remember: Promissory Note is not a valid mode of premium payment.

cards.title: Maximum Liability of Insurer
cards.content: The MAXIMUM LIMIT of the insurer's liability under the policy is the SUM INSURED. The insurer cannot be liable to pay more than the sum insured under any circumstances.

cards.title: What is a Cover Note?
cards.content: A Cover Note is a TEMPORARY CERTIFICATE issued when the preparation of the final policy document is still PENDING. It provides immediate evidence that the insurance contract has started, even before the full policy document is ready.

cards.title: Where is Cover Note Used?
cards.content: Cover Note is generally used in MARINE INSURANCE and MOTOR INSURANCE business. It is not applicable in all types of insurance — specific to these two categories.

cards.title: What is a Certificate of Insurance?
cards.content: Certificate of Insurance is a document that shows that the INSURANCE POLICY HAS BEEN WRITTEN (issued). For Motor Insurance specifically, the Certificate of Motor Insurance must ALWAYS BE KEPT IN THE VEHICLE (car/bike etc.) — it must always be carried with the vehicle.

cards.title: What is the Policy Document?
cards.content: The POLICY DOCUMENT is the FORMAL DOCUMENT that provides EVIDENCE that the insurance contract has commenced (started). It is the main contract document. It confirms all terms, conditions, coverage, and obligations of both parties.

cards.title: What is a Warranty?
cards.content: WARRANTY is a CONDITION that is EXPRESSLY STATED within the policy document itself. It must be literally complied with for the validity of the insurance contract. It is NOT a separate document — it is part of the policy document itself. Warranty = a condition written in the policy that must be strictly followed.

cards.title: What is Endorsement?
cards.content: ENDORSEMENT is the process of making MODIFICATIONS or CHANGES to the existing terms and conditions of an insurance policy. If the insured wants any change in the policy (e.g., change of address, change in sum insured), it is done through endorsement.

cards.title: What is a Renewal Notice?
cards.content: A RENEWAL NOTICE for motor insurance is issued by the INSURER (insurance company) BEFORE THE EXPIRY of the policy. It reminds the insured that their policy is about to expire and needs to be renewed.

sections.title: 🚀 Exam Pro-Tips — Chapter 1 General (Quick Memory)
items: First stage of insurance documentation = PROPOSAL FORM.
Declaration at end of proposal form = signed by INSURED.
Agent = INTERMEDIARY + PRIMARY UNDERWRITER / FIELD UNDERWRITER.
Underwriting = process of scrutinizing proposal and deciding acceptance.
IRDAI guideline: insurance company must process proposal within 15 DAYS.
Premium = CONSIDERATION = amount paid by INSURED to INSURER.
Premium can be paid: Cash, Cheque, Online, Credit Card. CANNOT be paid by Promissory Note.
Maximum liability of insurer = SUM INSURED.
Material Fact = information that INFLUENCES THE DECISION OF UNDERWRITER.
Fire proposal requires: process of manufacturing + details of materials + construction of building.
Cover Note = TEMPORARY certificate, issued when policy is PENDING. Used in MARINE and MOTOR insurance.
Certificate of Insurance = shows policy has been written.
Motor Certificate = must always be KEPT IN THE VEHICLE.
Policy Document = FORMAL EVIDENCE that insurance contract has commenced.
Warranty = condition EXPRESSLY STATED inside the policy document itself.
Endorsement = process of making CHANGES to existing policy terms.
Renewal Notice = issued by INSURER before policy expiry.
